hints: Notice weight $W$ and mass $m$ are given in mixed units such as $\text{mN}$, $\text{kN}$, $\text{g}$ and $\text{kg}$, so convert each to $\text{N}$ and $\text{kg}$ before comparing.
Recall that weight on a planet surface is $W = mg$, so the free-fall acceleration is the ratio $g = W/m$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
Calculate $W/m$ for all four rows and look for the smallest ratio, watching that the $2.6 \text{ kN}$ with $750 \text{ kg}$ row gives a surprisingly small value.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: weight is the gravitational force, $W = mg$, where $g$ is the acceleration of free fall at the planet surface.
Rearrange for comparison: $g = W/m$. The planet with the lowest $g$ has the smallest weight per unit mass.

Convert to SI units: A: $W = 40 \text{ mN} = 0.040 \text{ N}$, $m = 6.0 \text{ g} = 0.0060 \text{ kg}$. B: $W = 3.0 \text{ N}$, $m = 500 \text{ g} = 0.50 \text{ kg}$. C: $W = 10 \text{ N}$, $m = 1 \text{ kg}$. D: $W = 2.6 \text{ kN} = 2600 \text{ N}$, $m = 750 \text{ kg}$.
Compare the four $g$ values: $3.5 < 6.0 < 6.7 < 10$ in $\text{ m s}^{-2}$, so the D row is lowest. This is option D.
